review_notes: I read the whole file and the definitions it relies on: nsmulPt, mapPt, pushPt, FactorsThrough in Definitions/Def_CerednikDrinfeld_QMModuli.lean, and the schemeHomOverComp_coe variants. I ignored the long `attribute [-simp]` preamble because it appears in thousands of files, so it is shared boilerplate and not a problem specific to this file. I did not recommend `@[simp]` on comp_pushPt or comp_nsmulPt: the proof of `solution` uses them in both directions (`← comp_nsmulPt, ← comp_pushPt`, then `comp_pushPt, ..., comp_nsmulPt`), so a global orientation would conflict with one use. The only simp-interface gap I found is that nsmulPt has no named unfolding lemmas. As a result, the same `show ... from rfl` unfolding is written out by hand three times, and the same `hpow` bridge to `Monoid.npow` is proved twice. I could not run Lean, so I have not tested any of the proposed lemmas.

findings.problem: `nsmulPt` is a structurally recursive definition with no `nsmulPt_zero` or `nsmulPt_succ` lemmas. The file therefore unfolds it by hand with `show nsmulPt L t (k+1) X = L.mul t (nsmulPt L t k X) X from rfl` in the proofs of hom_nsmulPt, nsmulPt_nsmulPt and he_nsmul. The `zero` cases are closed with `exact L.one_natural ...` or `exact he_one` and rely on definitional unfolding. The identical `hpow : nsmulPt L t k X = X ^ k` induction is also proved twice, once in hom_nsmulPt and once in nsmulPt_nsmulPt. There is no stable rewrite interface for `nsmulPt`. Any proof about it must either unfold it by hand with `show ... from rfl` or use `simp [nsmulPt]`, which unfolds the whole definition.
findings.proposed_change: Next to `nsmulPt` in Definitions/Def_CerednikDrinfeld_QMModuli.lean, add `nsmulPt_zero : nsmulPt L t 0 P = L.one t` and `nsmulPt_succ : nsmulPt L t (n+1) P = L.mul t (nsmulPt L t n P) P`, both proved by `rfl`, and mark them `@[simp]`. They are terminating, since the argument shrinks, and they are not in conflict with any other rule. Also prove the bridge `nsmulPt L t n X = X ^ n` once, stated with the `L.pointGroup t` instance, as a named lemma. Then hom_nsmulPt, nsmulPt_nsmulPt and he_nsmul can use `nsmulPt_succ` and `nsmulPt_zero` instead of `show ... from rfl`, and the duplicated `hpow` block disappears.
findings.benefit: Proofs about `nsmulPt` can use `simp`/`rw` with named lemmas instead of repeating `show ... from rfl`. The duplicated `hpow` induction is stated once, so later changes to `nsmulPt` or its group instance need one edit and not several. I found no `nsmulPt_succ` or similar lemma in Definitions or Theorems, so the same `from rfl` pattern would have to be repeated in every downstream proof about `nsmulPt`.
